$comment: Høst: compound assignments such as += and >>>= in Go, Java, C++, PHP, TypeScript and JavaScript, and this before a private field (this.#x) in JavaScript and TypeScript, which the grammar leaves as a plain variable. Some of these grammars give them the same scope as =, others split them in two (^ and = in Java, &&= and ??= in TypeScript), so they would keep the text colour or be half coloured. They compute before they assign and get the structure colour like + and *, while = keeps the text colour. /= must follow a name, a number or a closing bracket, so that a regular expression such as /=/ is left alone. Applies outside strings, comments and JSX text.
